title: Account Retention Checklist + Deck Schematic (Standard & Enterprise)
content:
Purpose:
- Lightweight QBR deck template and operational checklist focused on retention and renewal readiness. Two variants: Standard (SMB / product-led accounts) and Enterprise (multi-stakeholder, contract renewal).
- Use as the default starting point for AMs before a quarterly review; keep <30 slides for enterprise, <12 slides for standard.

Audience and goals:
- Audience: CSM/AM, customer exec sponsor, engineering/product SME (as needed).
- Primary goals: demonstrate value delivered, identify adoption gaps, align on next 90-day outcomes, surface renewal ask and blockers.

Pre-QBR checklist (to run 7-10 days before meeting):
- Data pull: usage metrics (DAU, API calls, tokens, embedding calls), cost/savings signals, error rates.
- Health snapshot: compute health score (usage, infra errors, CSAT, support tickets) and trend vs last quarter.
- Renewal status: contract renewal date, T-minus days, expansion opportunities.
- Invite list: confirm executive sponsor + technical SME + procurement (for enterprise).
- Pre-read: 1-page value snapshot emailed 48h in advance.
- Runbook items: list of known product incidents or regressions to address proactively.

Quick presenter timing guide (Standard):
- 0–5 min: Check-in + agenda
- 5–15 min: Value recap (product usage + wins)
- 15–20 min: Adoption gaps + quick plan
- 20–25 min: Renewal conversation + ask
- 25–30 min: Next steps / action owners

Quick presenter timing guide (Enterprise):
- 0–7 min: Executive check-in + agenda
- 7–18 min: Value highlights (ROI, uptime, latency improvements, cost savings)
- 18–30 min: Deep dive on adoption & open technical risks
- 30–40 min: Roadmap alignment + proofs (security, compliance milestones)
- 40–50 min: Commercial conversation (renewal terms, expansion, pricing options)
- 50–60 min: Agreement on next steps, owners, dates

Slide-by-slide schematic (Standard, ~10 slides):
1. Cover slide: account, AM, date, quarter
2. One-line objective for meeting: e.g., "Align on Q2 outcomes and confirm renewal plan"
3. TL;DR (1 slide): 3 bullets — what we achieved, adoption trend, renewal status
4. Usage snapshot (visual): key metrics last 90 days vs prior quarter
5. Impact stories (2–3 short bullets): customer quotes, saved engineering time, feature adoption
6. Adoption gaps: 3 signal areas (feature X low, training needed, API errors) + mitigations
7. Roadmap / upcoming features: 2–3 items that matter to this customer
8. Renewal ask: options (auto-renew, 6/12/24 month), recommended next step and payment terms
9. Action log: owners, due dates, success criteria
10. Appendix pointers: support tickets, experiment outcomes, detailed usage CSV link

Slide-by-slide schematic (Enterprise, ~20–30 slides):
1. Cover + attendee roles table (exec sponsor, technical lead, procurement)
2. Meeting objective and intended outcome (decision or alignment)
3. Executive summary: 4-slide TL;DR (value, risks, financials, ask)
4. Business impact: ARR at risk/expansion, feature-led adoption charts, churn signals
5. Operational health: latency, throughput, error rate, incident cadence with timelines
6. Cost economics: per-token cost, caching/batching savings realized, forecasted savings with recommended config changes
7. Security & compliance posture: certs, SOC/ISO status, outstanding audits
8. Product roadmap alignment: items and expected delivery quarters
9. Case study: PoC or early adopter result inside the account
10. Migration/technical workplan: milestones, owners, blockers
11. SLA / reliability metrics: past quarter SLO attainment, RCA items
12. Commercial options: renewal scenarios, multi-year discounting, pilot-to-enterprise conversion pricing
13. Procurement checklist: data transfer agreements, KMS/HSM notes, SOC artifacts readiness
14. Executive ask slide: proposed contract language, decision deadline, recommended sign-off path
15. Risk register: prioritized risks with mitigation plan
16. Action register: owners, dates, success criteria (linked to ticket IDs)
17. Appendix: raw metrics, SRE notes, audit logs

Renewal tracker (plain-text table — copy into sheet for operational use):
Columns: Account | Renewal date | ARR | Current term | Health score (0-100) | Exec sponsor | Technical owner | Renewal risk (low/med/high) | Next step | Owner | Due date
Example rows (paste into sheet):
Redwood Retail Inc.|2025-10-10|$180,000|12m|78|Aisha Park|Tom Nguyen|medium|Send commercial options|Elena Martinez|2025-08-20
Sparkline Media|2025-06-01|$24,000|monthly|62|Mark O'Leary|Rita Patel|high|Schedule exec call + demo|Jamal Rivers|2025-05-05

Risk signals to watch (triggers that should escalate renewal outreach):
- 30% quarter-over-quarter drop in active usage
- Increase in incident tickets (>3 open >7 days)
- Exec sponsor changes or low NPS/CSAT in last 30 days
- Unresolved procurement/legal comments 45 days before renewal

Playbook actions (mapped to risk levels):
- Low risk: standard renewal email + one-pager value snapshot (owner: AM)
- Medium risk: schedule 1:1 with exec sponsor, propose targeted adoption plan (owner: CSM + Solutions Eng)
- High risk: escalate to Customer Success leadership, propose pilot-to-purchase incentives or time-limited discounts, align SRE and Product to clear blockers (owner: Head of CS)

Pre-crafted renewal language (email snippets):
- Standard: "Hi <Name>, happy to share a 1-page summary of value we've delivered this quarter and a recommended renewal path. Are you available for a 20-minute sync next week?"
- Enterprise: "Hi <Exec>, based on the outcomes we delivered and the roadmap alignment, we recommend transitioning to a 12-month committed plan. I propose a working session with procurement on <date> to align terms. Can you confirm availability?"

Appendix / AM notes (freeform):
- Notes to self: ask about SSO implementation timeline, confirm KMS rollout, flag pricing sensitivity.
- Links to artifacts: paste support ticket links, Confluence runbooks, recent incident RCAs.
- Quick checklist before sending deck: confirm numbers with finance, run deck through legal for pricing language, include compliance artifacts link for enterprise accounts.

Versioning and reuse guidance:
- Keep the top-level TL;DR concise — busy execs read the first slide.
- Maintain two templates in the drive: "standard" and "enterprise". Copy per account to maintain historical versions (date in footer).
- Use the renewal tracker sheet for live ownership and sync weekly with CS Ops.

Open questions / To iterate in this doc:
- Should we include a dedicated slide for model/regression quality monitoring outputs (embeddings drift, hallucination incidents)?
- How much pricing detail should be included in standard slides (keep simple vs full T&Cs)?

Deliverables for rollout:
- Export a one-page pre-read (PDF) generator from the template
- Create a short AM playbook checklist (2 pages) for pre-QBR preparation
- Build a weekly automation to update the renewal tracker from CRM (owner: CS Ops)

-- end --
